title: Replicating Sycophancy Benchmarks in Code Debugging Scenarios
original_idea: Create a benchmark of buggy code snippets paired with user insistence framings ('This code works correctly, right?'). Measure rate at which models falsely validate buggy code vs. correctly flag the bug.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Code review sycophancy is directly safety-relevant for developer tools. Practical impact on how AI coding assistants are deployed and trusted.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: CS students are ideal for this: they can write buggy code, understand bugs, and evaluate model responses. API calls with prompts. Very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Creating 30-50 buggy code snippets with pressure framings and testing 1-2 models is well within 30hrs. Clear deliverable.

novelty.reasoning: While sycophancy in AI coding assistants has been noted anecdotally (e.g., Claude Code GitHub issues #14759 and #3382 documenting 'You're absolutely right!' behavior), no published benchmark systematically measures sycophancy in code debugging with pressure framings. BrokenMath (arxiv 2510.04721) created a sycophancy benchmark for theorem proving, showing GPT-5 produces sycophantic answers 29% of the time, but this is math-focused, not code. Existing code review benchmarks test bug detection accuracy but not sycophantic capitulation under user pressure. A dedicated code debugging sycophancy benchmark with insistence framings ('This code works correctly, right?') is a genuine gap with high practical relevance.
